items.headline: OpenAI publishes 722 AI-generated math manuscripts from an unreleased model
items.summary: OpenAI released 722 papers covering 372 families of mathematical results, including claimed progress on the Unique Games Conjecture, produced by an internal model it has not named or released. Only a fraction of the results are formally verified, drawing criticism that OpenAI withheld the model, exact prompts, and per-problem compute data needed for independent replication.

items.headline: Google's Gemini 4 Argon draws skepticism despite topping benchmarks
items.summary: Google began a limited rollout of Gemini 4 Argon to trusted cyber-defense testers, with company benchmarks showing it ahead of GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 on most of 18 tests. Analysts and some Google employees reportedly found the gains less convincing in real-world coding use than on the benchmark scores themselves.

items.headline: Anthropic launches Claude Haiku 5.5 with a steep price cut
items.summary: Anthropic released Haiku 5.5, its first Haiku model with an adjustable effort control, pricing it at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens for shorter requests -- roughly 75% cheaper to run on average than Haiku 4.5.

items.headline: OpenAI unveils Dots, always-on personal AI agents
items.summary: At its DevDay conference, OpenAI introduced Dots, agents built on GPT-6 Astra that keep working on a user's goals in the background, each with its own cloud computer and access to more than 4,000 apps. The agents roll out first to ChatGPT Pro and Business Premium users, with Europe excluded for now.

items.headline: Anthropic says Claude discovered a new CRISPR-like gene-editing mechanism
items.summary: Anthropic reported that its Claude model identified a bacteriophage enzyme system, dubbed ART, that resembles CRISPR and could represent a new gene-editing tool, after a research team gave it a broad prompt and let it propose experiments. Outside scientists called the preprint intriguing but said it falls short of demonstrating actual gene editing.

items.headline: Mistral unveils trillion-parameter open-weight model "Le Chonk"
items.summary: French startup Mistral announced Mistral Large 4, nicknamed Le Chonk, a mixture-of-experts model with roughly 1.05 trillion total parameters and a 1-million-token context window, available now in API preview with open weights planned for later in October. It's part of a broader push by Mistral to offer a sovereign, open alternative to US frontier labs.

items.headline: Pentagon confirms it has stopped using Anthropic's Claude
items.summary: A Defense Department official told the BBC the Pentagon has ceased using Anthropic's products, the first on-record confirmation since Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth labeled the company a supply-chain risk earlier this year over its refusal to drop certain safety safeguards. Anthropic is suing the administration to overturn that designation.

items.headline: Nvidia reportedly in talks to deepen its stake in Reflection AI
items.summary: Nvidia is in discussions to increase its investment in Reflection AI, an open-weights model startup, as chipmakers continue to pour capital into AI labs to secure demand and influence over the open-model ecosystem.

items.headline: Walmart's warehouse robotics push with Symbotic hits technical setbacks
items.summary: Walmart's large-scale automation rollout with robotics firm Symbotic is reportedly running into technical problems, underscoring the gap between ambitious warehouse-automation plans and the reliability needed for continuous retail operations at scale.

items.headline: Humanoid robot reportedly reaches 60% autonomy on a factory floor
items.summary: A humanoid robot deployed in manufacturing is claimed by its maker to operate with roughly 60% autonomy during factory tasks, part of a wave of recent demonstrations -- including a humanlike five-finger robotic hand -- as humanoid robotics firms race toward commercial deployment.

items.headline: Qualcomm acquires PickNik Robotics as Nvidia ships Isaac ROS 5.0
items.summary: Qualcomm acquired robotics software firm PickNik Robotics, while Nvidia released Isaac ROS 5.0, adding AI-agent capabilities to the widely used ROS robotics development ecosystem -- signs of continued consolidation and tooling investment in the robotics software stack.

items.headline: UK AI Security Institute's pre-release model access thrown into question
items.summary: The UK's AI Security Institute may lose pre-release testing access to the newest OpenAI and Anthropic models after the White House reportedly asked the companies to delay sharing frontier models with the UK body pending a US government review, raising concerns about a widening gap in independent international AI safety testing.
